endorsements.quote: In addition, the import of data from internal clinical systems such as the hospital information system (HIS), the radiological information system (RIS) and PACS must be guaranteed.

endorsements.title: Improving Sepsis Prediction in the ICU with Explainable Artificial Intelligence: The Promise of Bayesian Networks
endorsements.quote: Integration with electronic health records via standard medical data communication protocols (HL7, FHIR, etc.) would make it possible to automatically retrieve the necessary information (vital signs, tests) and return the probability calculation in the form of an alert in the patient’s electronic health record.

evidence.title: AI adoption and workflow optimization following orchestration platform implementation and structured change management
evidence.outcome: Radiologist user-verification rate of AI outputs
evidence.effect: Verification rose from 13.9% (318/2287) at baseline to 61.1% (1778/2910) after orchestration platform plus change management; full verification of multi-task exams 62.6%; 9480 AI tasks across 12 applications.
evidence.quote: The overall user-verification rate increased from 13.9% (318/2287) at baseline to 61.1% (1778/2910) after implementation, while full verification of examinations containing multiple AI tasks increased to 62.6%.

evidence.title: Improving Turnaround Times with Artificial Intelligence in Microbiology
evidence.outcome: Urine culture turnaround time following automatic release of results to patient charts
evidence.effect: PM+ automatic result release further improved turnaround time beyond PM; the additional reduction was not quantified.
evidence.quote: Implementation of PM+, which automatically releases defined results to patient charts, further improved turnaround time.

evidence.title: Integrated Implementation Strategies to Promote the Use of AI-Assisted Diagnostic Software for Lung Nodule Screening in China: Process Evaluation Based on the RE-AIM Framework
evidence.outcome: Successful automated transfer of CT images and AI results between hospitals
evidence.effect: CT image transmission succeeded for 90.9% (20/22); two patients experienced PACS-related transmission failures and were required to carry physical CT films to the tertiary hospital.
evidence.quote: Despite a relatively high CT image transmission success rate of 90.9% (20/22), system-level failures persisted.

evidence.title: Triaging mammography with artificial intelligence: an implementation study
evidence.outcome: Failures of AI integration with site software
evidence.effect: AI integration with site software failed in 3 cases due to a software error.
evidence.quote: In 3 cases AI integration with site software failed due to a software error.

evidence.title: Increasing Advance Care Planning Discussions and Documentation
evidence.venue: Journal of the advanced practitioner in oncology
evidence.outcome: Patients missed by model routing because of inaccurate admitting-service classification
evidence.effect: Some patients inaccurately admitted under “hematology” were not captured. In November 2022, model eligibility expanded to both services; the missed-patient count was not reported.
evidence.quote: In November 2022, the model was again adjusted to include patients with hematologic malignancies admitted under both the “hematology” and “hematology oncology” service, since data analysis indicated some patients were inaccurately admitted under the “hematology” service and had thus not been captured by the model.

evidence.title: Integrated Implementation Strategies to Promote the Use of AI-Assisted Diagnostic Software for Lung Nodule Screening in China: Process Evaluation Based on the RE-AIM Framework
evidence.effect: Two of the 22 successfully referred patients experienced data transmission failures that prevented the upload of AI-generated results and images.
evidence.quote: Among the 22 patients who successfully completed the referral process, two experienced data transmission failures due to PACS system malfunctions at the secondary hospital, which prevented the upload of AI-generated results and CT images to the ESDR platform.

commentary.bottom_line: Two uncontrolled before-after studies suggest that automated routing may shorten result turnaround and usually delivers images and AI outputs between sites, but transmission still failed for 2 of 22 referred patients in one study. The evidence favors automation paired with checks for failed transfers, and certainty is very low.

perspectives.view: Two before-after studies without comparators test the practice. One reports shorter urine culture turnaround after automatic result release but does not quantify the added effect. The other reports successful CT transfer for 90.9% (20/22) of patients. Risk of bias, indirectness, and imprecision each lower certainty, which leaves it at very low.

Hazard studies show that data flows fail in real deployments. A randomized trial recorded 3 AI integration failures from a software error, and another deployment missed patients whose admitting service was misclassified. These studies show that the problem exists, not that automation prevents it. The China study suggests that automated transfer still needs a way to detect failed uploads.

The Canadian study suggests that sending results directly into the chart may reduce delay beyond process changes alone. In a separate deployment, routing missed patients because eligibility depended on one admitting service, and the team widened eligibility in November 2022. Automated routing depends on the accuracy of the upstream fields it reads.

Neither study that tests the practice reports cost, staff time, or interface maintenance effort. The China deployment covered 1291 patients and still relied on a manual fallback, physical films, when PACS transfer failed. Health systems adopting automated routing may need to budget for failure alerts and a staffed backup path.

When automated transfer failed in the China study, two patients had to carry physical CT films to the tertiary hospital. This finding suggests that failed data flows can shift work and delay onto patients. Patients may be better served when a staff member confirms that results arrived and patients know whom to contact when they do not.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares automated routing with manual routing using a concurrent control group, and none reports how often wrong studies or wrong patients reach a model. Future studies could measure misrouting, undelivered results, and time to result delivery across several sites and report the size of each effect.
commentary.underserved_note: Neither study that tests the practice reports enrolling or analyzing Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. The evidence therefore does not show whether automated routing performs as well in safety-net settings, where interface resources and record linkage may differ.
